title: Shift Baton: compact timeline transfer flow for SLO-aware alert handoffs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Engineers regularly miss context during shift changes. Existing alert cards surface SLO deltas but require multiple clicks to attach runbooks, cost snapshots, and postmortem links. We need a compact transfer flow that minimizes cognitive switching during handoffs while preserving actionability (ack, assign, escalate) and surfacing cost and SLO context inline.
goal: Design a compact 'Shift Baton' timeline strip and a guided transfer composer that: 1) surfaces SLO drift snapshot and cost delta for the last 24h, 2) provides inline runbook snippets and one-click postmortem deep-links, 3) supports graceful transfer with a confirmation gesture and short microcopy for incoming engineer, and 4) is usable on narrow screens and mobile on-call views.
constraints: Must fit into existing console alert list row height without vertical redraw, leverage existing SLO snapshot API, show only top 3 cost contributors, and respect RBAC (no postmortem link if user lacks view permissions). Interaction must be accessible (keyboard + screen reader).
proposed_screens: 1) Compact baton strip appended to alert row with mini-graph (SLO trajectory), cost delta pill, and transfer button. 2) Transfer composer modal with recipient picker, short message field, suggested runbook snippets, and auto-attached postmortem link (if available). 3) Compact timeline view for the recipient with collapsed events, highlighted SLO delta, and an 'accept baton' affordance.
microcopy_examples: Transfer button tooltip: 'Pass shift baton — include SLO & cost snapshot'. Confirmation prompt: 'Hand off to {name}? A brief note will be sent; you can add runbook snippets.' Incoming card header: 'Shift received — context summary'.
acceptance_criteria:
- Transfer completes with a single confirmation and creates an immutable handoff entry in the incident timeline.
- SLO snapshot and cost delta visible without opening modal.
- Runbook snippets insert as inline references and link to full runbook.
- Accessibility: modal reachable via keyboard; baton button has ARIA label.
- Analytics events emitted for transfer, accept, and view actions.
design_decisions: 1) Use a horizontal micro-timeline to preserve vertical space instead of expanding rows. 2) Show only top contributors to cost rather than full breakdown to avoid clutter. 3) Provide a suggested message generated from the recent incident notes with an edit affordance. 4) Make postmortem link optional for users lacking permission; show placeholder with 'request access' action.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: extra controls increase cognitive load on small screens. Mitigation: collapse advanced details behind a chevron; default state shows only baton, SLO pill, and transfer icon. Risk: inaccurate cost snapshot at high scale. Mitigation: show stale timestamp and link to live cost explorer.
usability_findings: Session testing (n=8, cross-platform) produced: 1) median transfer time 6.2s when using suggested message, 2) 2 participants missed the 'accept baton' affordance on narrow screens so we increased the contrast and added a bounce affordance, 3) users valued immediate SLO delta in the row and used it to decide whether to transfer.
next_steps: 1) Finalize token microcopy and ARIA labels (design). 2) Engineering to implement baton row and composer API contract (ENG-29144). 3) PM to scope analytic events and success metrics (time-to-ack, transfer adoption). 4) Ship dark-mode polish and mobile collapse behavior in console-2026.04.
